# rmskProfiler

<!-- badges: start -->
<!-- badges: end -->

rmskProfiler quantifies transposable elements (TEs) at the locus level from
RNA-seq data and imports the counts into R for downstream analysis. It:

1. builds a [Salmon](https://salmon.readthedocs.io) index from GENCODE
   transcripts, the unique sequences of RepeatMasker TE loci, and the genome as
   a decoy,
2. quantifies reads against this index with Gibbs sampling, and
3. imports the quantifications as an annotated `SummarizedExperiment`, with the
   counts scaled for the uncertainty from multi-mapping reads.

TE loci with identical sequences cannot be told apart by any read, so they are
collapsed into a single target named by the SHA1 hash of the sequence. The
annotation records all the loci that share each hash, their RepeatMasker
classifications, and the genomic features (exons, introns, UTRs, promoters)
they overlap.

## Installation

You can install the development version of rmskProfiler from
[GitHub](https://github.com/coriell-research/rmskProfiler) with:

``` r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("coriell-research/rmskProfiler")
```

Building the index and quantifying reads requires a recent version of
[Salmon](https://salmon.readthedocs.io/en/latest/building.html#binary-releases)
on your `PATH`. Importing and analysing quantifications does not.

Building the index also requires the BSgenome package of the genome sequence:

``` r
BiocManager::install("BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38") # human
BiocManager::install("BSgenome.Mmusculus.UCSC.mm10") # mouse
```

## Quick start

The whole workflow for human RNA-seq samples takes three steps, plus an
optional fourth:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(rmskProfiler)

# 1. Build the index (once per species). This downloads the GENCODE v48 GTF,
#    extracts the transcript and unique RepeatMasker TE sequences from
#    BSgenome.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg38, annotates the TEs, and builds a Salmon index
#    of transcripts + TEs with the genome as a decoy. Files are kept in the
#    rmskProfiler cache, the index is written to "hg38-salmon_index".
generateIndex("hg38-salmon_index", species = "Hs", threads = 12)

# 2. Quantify reads with Salmon using Gibbs sampling. This can also be done
#    outside of R, as long as Salmon is run with --numGibbsSamples
salmonQuant(
    fq1 = c("sample1.R1.fq.gz", "sample2.R1.fq.gz"),
    fq2 = c("sample1.R2.fq.gz", "sample2.R2.fq.gz"),
    sample_names = c("sample1", "sample2"),
    index_dir = "hg38-salmon_index",
    out_dir = "quants",
    n_gibbs = 30,
    "--threads 12"
)

# 3. Import transcript and TE locus counts as an annotated
#    SummarizedExperiment, with counts scaled for multi-mapping uncertainty
se <- importQuants("quants", species = "Hs")

# 4. (Optional) Sum transcripts to genes and TE loci to subfamilies
aggregated <- aggregateCounts(se, species = "Hs", te_level = "subfamily")

# Inspect, locate, or remove the cached files
listResources()
```

Aggregation is not required for differential expression analysis. Both `se`
and `aggregated` are standard `SummarizedExperiment` objects that can be used
directly with Bioconductor packages for differential expression testing, such
as edgeR and limma.

By default, RepeatMasker records shorter than 32 bp and those with classes
"Simple_repeat", "Low_complexity", "Satellite", "RNA", "rRNA", "snRNA",
"scRNA", "srpRNA", "tRNA", and "Unknown" are excluded from the index. Use the
`exclude` and `min_len` arguments to change this, and pass the same values to
`importQuants()`.

## Learn more

The package vignette walks through the whole workflow on example data included
with the package, and covers:

- running Salmon outside of R,
- the annotations stored in the imported `SummarizedExperiment`,
- filtering TE loci and transcripts and aggregating counts to genes and TE
  subfamilies, families, or classes,
- differential expression testing with edgeR or limma,
- the resources stored in the rmskProfiler cache and how to manage them.

Read the vignette source in
[vignettes/rmskProfiler.Rmd](vignettes/rmskProfiler.Rmd), or install the package
with its vignette and open it from R:

``` r
remotes::install_github(
    "coriell-research/rmskProfiler",
    dependencies = TRUE,
    build_vignettes = TRUE
)
vignette("rmskProfiler")
```
